title: UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London – July 8, 2025
excerpt: A landmark UKPNP International Kashmir Conference was held in the Houses of Parliament, London, addressing peace, security, human rights, and the reunification of the forcibly divided State of Jammu and Kashmir.
author: Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan

heroImage.caption: UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, Boothroyd Room, House of Commons, London

body.text: UKPNP International Conference on Jammu & Kashmir – House of Commons, London

The United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP) convened a major international conference in the Boothroyd Room of the Houses of Parliament, London, focusing on peace, security, and fundamental rights in Jammu and Kashmir. The event brought together Members of Parliament, human rights defenders, legal experts, academics, media professionals, and diaspora representatives.
“Kashmir is not a territorial or bilateral issue. It is an international issue.” – Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri

The conference was hosted by Richard Burgon MP, Labour MP for Leeds East and former Shadow Secretary of State for Justice. The keynote address was delivered by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Exiled Chairman of UKPNP and Administrative Director of CIRAC to the United Nations. The session was presided over by Sardar Tariq Khan, President UKPNP UK, and moderated by Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson of UKPNP and Main Representative to the UN in Geneva and New York.
UKPNP has consistently opposed violence, terrorism, extremism, and the weaponization of faith.

body.caption: Panel session during the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference

body.text: The conference featured participation from Fabian Hamilton MP, Imran Hussain MP, and Ian Byrne MP, alongside senior UKPNP leaders and representatives of oppressed nations. Speakers included Dr. Shabir Chaudhry, Mahmood Ahmed Kashmiri, Mrs. Faria Attique, Raja Sarfraz Khan, Sajjad Hussain, Sohail Talat, Syeda Mahroona Bukhari, Syed Barkatul Hasan, Mushahid Manzoor, and many others.
“Self-determination is a fundamental right which Kashmiris deserve.” – Ian Byrne MP
Condemnation of Pahalgam Terror Attack and Extrajudicial Killings

Speakers condemned the Pahalgam terror attack that claimed the lives of at least 26 civilians. They honored Adil Shah, a Kashmiri who sacrificed his life protecting tourists. The conference also condemned the extrajudicial killings of Zarnosh Nasim and Jibran Nasim in Rawalakot, calling for an independent judicial inquiry.

body.caption: Zarnosh Nasim, one of the victims of extrajudicial killings in Rawalakot

body.text: UKPNP demands an immediate end to extrajudicial killings, torture, enforced disappearances, and misuse of anti-terror laws.
Demand for Release of Political Prisoners

The conference demanded the release of political prisoners across Jammu and Kashmir, including Mumtaz Nagari, Advocate Ehsan Ali, Advocate Taaruf Abbas, Sher Nadir Shahi, and Muhammad Nafees. Speakers highlighted the alarming rise in enforced disappearances and kidnapping of minors, urging accountability and recovery of missing children.
“We demand freedom of expression, movement, reunification, and the right to self-determination for all.” – Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri

body.caption: Delegates discussing human rights and regional security

text.text: Human Rights, Civil Liberties, and Rule of Law

The conference reaffirmed its commitment to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and called for an end to arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, and restrictions on freedoms across all regions of Jammu and Kashmir. Delegates highlighted the cases of Zarnosh Nasim and Jibran Nasim, whose deaths raised serious concerns about accountability and rule of law.
“We demand a judicial inquiry into extrajudicial killings and the alarming rise in enforced disappearances.”
Participants and Delegates

The conference was attended by a wide range of activists, community leaders, journalists, and diaspora members including Sardar Amjad Yousaf, Sardar Tikka Khan Tahir, Yasir Arfat Qureshi, Naveed Khan, Aftan Hussain, Jamil Latif, Farooq Nazir, Muhammad Ramzan, Ishaq Khan, Muhammad Gaffar Hussain, Irfan Ashfaq, Hamza Shakeel, Muhammad Nisar, Muhammad Anis, Shafique ur Rehman, Syed Altaf Hussain, Abdul Rehman, Gul Zaman, Muhammad Ijaz Khan, Mahmood Ahmed, Qamar Khalil, Abdul Satar, Zarak Aftab, Usman Khan, Muhammad Adnan Khan, Qamar Farooq, Iftikhar Waqas, Arif Ajakia, Syed Taqdees Ali Gilani, Mehtab Subhani, Muhammad Shehbaz, Syed Farzad Gilani, Saiq Shah, Abdul Aziz Sheen, Sohail Aqeel, Haidher Aftab, Ashfaq Sadiq, Raja Yasir Sayab, Ishtiaq Sadiq, Musa Sadiq, Salar Saeed, Maqsood Kiyani, Waqar Aziz, Shezad Afzal, Syeda Tousifa Haider Gilani, Malik Sajid Hussain, Maria Mehwish, Zohaib Khan, Hina Javaid, Raja Muhammad Habib, Moseeb Khan, Zaheer Ahmed Kiyani, Saqib Khan, Akash Khan, Hashir Abbasi, Muhammad Rukshad Khan, and Naqeer Ahmed.

text.text: Democratic Governance and Political Participation

Speakers stressed the need for democratic freedoms across all regions of Jammu and Kashmir, calling for the restoration of constitutional safeguards, protection of civil liberties, and an end to the suppression of political dissent. The conference demanded the immediate release of all political prisoners and the cessation of intimidation and harassment of activists and journalists.
“No part of Jammu and Kashmir should be used to conduct proxy wars or spread ideological radicalization.”
Terrorism, Extremism, and Regional Stability

The conference condemned all forms of terrorism and extremism, urging authorities to prevent radicalization and violence. Delegates emphasized the need to protect cultural, linguistic, and religious identities across all regions, and called for sustainable development policies that respect local rights and resources.
International Engagement and Diaspora Involvement

The conference appealed to the United Kingdom, United Nations, European Union, and other international institutions to support a peaceful and rights-based resolution of the Kashmir conflict. It recommended the appointment of a UN Special Rapporteur and encouraged multi-stakeholder dialogue involving all regions and communities.
“A lasting and just peace can only be achieved through justice, accountability, and inclusive dialogue.”
Monitoring, Implementation, and Working Group

UKPNP proposed the creation of an International Kashmir Peace and Human Rights Working Group to monitor developments, propose peaceful solutions, and submit annual reports to the British Parliament and international forums.
Reunification, Buffer State, and No Military Solution

The conference reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir must be reunified as a peaceful, autonomous buffer state between India, Pakistan, and China. Delegates emphasized that there is no military solution to the conflict and that forced divisions and unilateral decisions have only deepened suffering.
“The historical State of Jammu and Kashmir should be reunified and declared a buffer state between three nuclear powers.”
Concluding Remarks

UKPNP leadership thanked MP Richard Burgon and all participating MPs for their support. Moderator Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan highlighted that this was the fourth consecutive UKPNP international conference held in the House of Commons. The party reaffirmed its peaceful and democratic mission for reunification and fundamental rights.

British MPs reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir is an international issue, not a bilateral dispute, and that UN resolutions remain relevant. They emphasized that the future of the region must be determined in accordance with international law and the aspirations of the people.
